growth_story.headline: Suriname's gold-led rise ended in 2013; a commodity bust and a 2020 fiscal crisis left income per person 21.4 percent below its peak, with oil due in 2028.
growth_story.arc: Suriname's income per person shrank by 1.0 percent a year over 1990–2000, a decade the IMF links to political turmoil, policy missteps and bouts of near-hyperinflation. From 2001 to 2013 it grew 3.3 percent a year, as stronger policies and political stability met high commodity prices and gold became the main export, and it peaked in 2013. Since 2014 it has fallen 1.8 percent a year: gold and oil prices dropped from 2015, alumina production stopped, and a fiscal and balance-of-payments crisis, made worse by COVID-19, brought a fall of 16.9 percent in 2020. Modest gains since 2022 have left income per person 21.4 percent below its 2013 peak, about where it first was in 1977. Both the IMF and the World Bank now describe an economy waiting on offshore oil, due to start in 2028, while gold output has weakened.

threads.title: Turmoil before 2000
threads.text: Before 2000, growth swung widely and inflation at times came close to hyperinflation. The IMF ties this to political turmoil and policy mistakes, and income per person shrank 1.0 percent a year over 1990–2000.

citations.title: Suriname: 2013 Article IV Consultation (IMF Country Report No. 13/340)
citations.quote: The period prior to 2000 was marred by large swings in GDP growth and episodes of near-hyperinflation, reflecting political turmoil and policy missteps.

threads.title: Gold drives the 2000s boom
threads.text: After 2000, stronger policies and political stability met high commodity prices. Gold went from a small share of exports to the dominant one, and income per person grew 3.3 percent a year from 2001 to 2013.

citations.title: Suriname: 2013 Article IV Consultation (IMF Country Report No. 13/340)
citations.quote: Since 2000, however, stronger policies and buoyant commodity prices, supported by political stability, have improved macroeconomic performance

citations.title: Suriname: 2013 Article IV Consultation (IMF Country Report No. 13/340)
citations.quote: gold, which currently accounts for about 67 percent of exports compared to only 7 percent ten years ago

threads.title: Commodity bust, then 2020 crisis
threads.text: From 2015 gold and oil prices fell and alumina production stopped; income per person fell in 2014, 2015 and 2016. A short recovery in 2017–2019 gave way to a fiscal and balance-of-payments crisis in 2020, made worse by COVID-19, when income per person fell 16.9 percent.

citations.title: Country Partnership Framework for Suriname for the Period FY25-FY29
citations.quote: The price of gold and oil declined, and alumina production came to a halt, causing a shock to the economy

citations.title: Country Partnership Framework for Suriname for the Period FY25-FY29
citations.quote: Notwithstanding the positive economic developments between 2017-2019, a severe fiscal and balance of payments crisis began to unfold in Suriname in 2020

citations.title: Country Partnership Framework for Suriname for the Period FY25-FY29
citations.quote: This dire situation was compounded by the COVID-19 pandemic, and the subsequent closure of borders for approximately 18 months

threads.title: Stabilization, then slippage
threads.text: An IMF-supported program rebuilt reserves, brought inflation down and put debt on a sustainable path. Spending ahead of the May 2025 election then undid a large part of the budget tightening.

citations.title: Suriname: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Statement by the Executive Director for Suriname (IMF Country Report No. 26/37)
citations.quote: Reserves had been rebuilt, inflation was reduced to single digits, debt was put on a sustainable path

citations.title: Suriname: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Statement by the Executive Director for Suriname (IMF Country Report No. 26/37)
citations.quote: Expenditure rose significantly prior to the May election, unwinding a significant portion of fiscal adjustment that was undertaken as part of the Fund-supported program

threads.title: Gold fades, oil approaches
threads.text: Gold output fell in 2024 and stayed weak in the first half of 2025, with more reported smuggling by small miners and harder geology at large mines. Oil production from the offshore field is expected to begin in 2028.

citations.title: Suriname: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Statement by the Executive Director for Suriname (IMF Country Report No. 26/37)
citations.quote: Gold production declined by 8 percent in 2024 and continued to disappoint in the first half of 2025.

citations.title: Suriname: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Statement by the Executive Director for Suriname (IMF Country Report No. 26/37)
citations.quote: Gold smuggling by small miners has reportedly increased, and large mining companies are facing a less favorable geology.

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: Suriname (October 2026)
citations.quote: Growth is projected to improve in 2026–27 and rise substantially in 2028 as oil production begins.

since_last_year.text: Loose budget and money policy in 2025 weakened the currency and pushed inflation back into double digits. By early 2026 activity had picked up sharply as work on the offshore oil field spread into construction, trade and financial services.

citations.title: Suriname: 2025 Article IV Consultation—Press Release; Staff Report; Staff Statement; and Statement by the Executive Director for Suriname (IMF Country Report No. 26/37)
citations.quote: fiscal and monetary slippages in 2025 reduced cash buffers, weakened the currency, and increased inflation back to double digits

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: Suriname (October 2026)
citations.quote: The monthly economic activity index increased by 11.9 percent year-on-year in January–April 2026, compared with 0.2 percent over the same period in 2025.

citations.title: Macro Poverty Outlook: Suriname (October 2026)
citations.quote: Construction, trade, and financial services expanded strongly, supported by demand related to oil-project preparations.

growth_story.tension: The sources describe strong activity in early 2026 and a coming oil boom, but through 2025 the data show income per person still 21.4 percent below its 2013 peak, growing only 0.8 to 1.5 percent a year since 2022.
